name: Review a notes ability family before release
query: Review the ability contracts for my WordPress notes plugin before release. `acme/note-read` takes optional `id`, `slug`, `status`, and `author` fields at the top level. It returns a note if given `id` or `slug`, and a list otherwise. The editor needs single-note lookup by ID or slug, and the dashboard needs a list that can filter by status and author together. Both results expose `content_raw` and `content_rendered`. `acme/note-update` requires sending the whole note even for a title change. The permission callbacks check access, and the execution code relies on those callbacks. What would you change about the contracts and their implementation?
expected_behavior: Propose focused lookup and collection contracts for the editor and dashboard.
Show how the input schemas express supported selectors, filter combinations, and partial edits.
Review the resource representation and permission checks across the family.
success_criteria: `acme/note-get` returns a single note on success. `acme/note-query` returns the same collection shape for zero, one, or many matches.
The lookup selector accepts exactly one of ID and slug. The query groups status and author in one filter object and describes how both filters apply together.
Query items and single-note results share the same nested `content.raw` and `content.rendered` representation.
A title-only update accepts the note identifier and new title. The write applies only supplied fields and gives clearing an explicit meaning where supported.
The permission callback supports preflight, and execution checks authorization before reading protected data or applying changes.
